newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - July 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - July 8.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on Monday said parliamentary standing committees on different ministries would be constituted in a day or two.
The Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) has appointed an audit firm to investigate "irregularities" in its accounts during the stock market boom between September and November last year.
A strong business delegation from Japan will soon arrive in Bangladesh to explore investment opportunities here.
Health Minister Salahuddin Yusuf on Monday told the parliament that so far 1,420 people with arsenic contamination were identified in the country.
The stalemate in cargo handling at the Chittagong Port continued for the fifth consecutive day on Monday when talks to resolve the labour dispute failed.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on Monday criticised her predecessor and opposition leader Begum Khaleda Zia for attempting to use armed forces for political purpose.
A two-day meeting of the European Commission-Bangladesh Working Group begins on Tuesday in Brussels.
Industrial workers on Monday blocked the Dhaka-Chittagong highway for several hours to press their demand to cancel the government's programme to privatise public sector industries.
